author: reek
body: `Real saturating` clamps a result that leaves the finite range to the largest finite magnitude of the same sign, and answers zero for a NaN.

author: reek
body: This test used to add 3.0 and 4.0 and divide zero by zero, and that is all. Neither case leaves the finite range, so it exercised the arithmetic and never the mode: the emitter clamped nothing at all, and an overflow returned a plain infinity for as long as the mode has existed. A test that cannot reach the behaviour it names is the shape ExaminersAssay calls a function that always answers the same thing.

author: reek
body: The operands are built from bit patterns rather than written as decimals because the largest finite double has no short decimal form, and a literal close to it would test a different number than the one at the boundary.

author: reek
body: Answers are compared as bit patterns. The difference between the largest finite double and infinity is one in the last place of the exponent field, and every decimal rendering of the two that this compiler can produce looks identical.

author: reek
body: Each line names what the mode must do. The finite cases are controls: a mode that clamped everything, or that had simply replaced arithmetic with a constant, would fail them.
